idiom_name: Ktor Application + install(plugin) pipeline + routing plugin
implementation_notes: Ktor's front controller is the Application pipeline: startup installs plugins that wrap every call (logging, CORS, compression, authentication) and routing itself is a plugin that dispatches to handlers, with plugins also installable per route for scoped behaviour. What replaces the classic structure: the plugin pipeline replaces the FrontController class and its pre/post hooks, and the routing DSL replaces a command registry; Ktor documents routing as nothing more than a plugin inside the same request/response pipeline. Spring Boot and Javalin offer the same roles with different APIs.
pitfalls: Plugin install order defines the wrapper order, and a route-scoped install overrides the global configuration - duplicating a CORS or compression install silently changes behaviour (last installation wins).
Handlers are suspend functions over shared state; a blocking JDBC or file call inside them starves the dispatcher unless moved to Dispatchers.IO.
Responding twice (or responding after a plugin already ended the call) throws; a short-circuiting plugin must end the call explicitly and predictably.
